title: A long yes to the said-back prediction moment builds, instead of being said back as a new moment
request: The owner, in a cloud session: review the repository after 37.11 (the lead agent as Home's default) and track the approved plan (build path, route, speed, final test, cost).
spec: Step 0 of the plan says the build path must work end to end with no trade allowed. When Home says the prediction moment back, any yes builds; a correction (but, instead, rather, actually, a leading no) is said back again; a hold on the build builds nothing.
plan: Read the 37.11 diff against the plan's step 0
Probe the confirm-moment step with natural answers outside the tests
Write failing tests for the answers that loop
Narrow the correction words, add the hold, keep the said-back correction
Run the affected tests, record, rebuild the dev SFT set

decisions.decision: A yes of any length builds; the length rule (more than four words means a correction) is removed
decisions.why: full-sentence yeses are common ("Yes, that is correct, go ahead") and were said back as the moment, so the person looped

decisions.decision: Only but, instead, rather, actually or a leading no/nope/not mark a correction
decisions.why: a no or not later in a yes ("Yes, no other changes") is not a new moment

decisions.decision: A hold on the build ("hold off", "not yet ... build") drops the question and the agent reads the words
decisions.why: with "but" now a correction, "yes, but hold off" would otherwise be said back as a moment

change: dclab_rnd/draft/case_home.py (CORRECTION narrowed, HOLD_BUILD and LEADING_ANSWER added, the confirm-moment branch); tests/test_case_home.py (two tests)

findings.defect: A long yes to the said-back moment was taken as a new moment
findings.scenario: Home: "So the prediction is made at checkout ... Shall I build with that?" Person: "Yes, that is correct, go ahead". Home: "So the prediction is made that is correct, go ahead, using only what is known then. Shall I build with that?" and again on every full-sentence yes
findings.cause: the confirm step treated any yes longer than four words as a correction, stripped the leading yes and said the rest back as the moment; a bare "no" or "not" anywhere also counted as a correction
findings.fix: a correction only on but/instead/rather/actually or a leading no; a hold builds nothing; any other yes builds

outcome: The build path's last step no longer loops on a full-sentence yes. Not measured live: the 37.11 live check never reached the build's moment question.
lessons: A rule that reads a person's words needs probing with natural answers, not only the ones its tests were written from
Length is a weak signal for meaning: a long yes is still a yes
risks: The moment question still takes any non-question of three or more words as the moment ("Let me check with my team" is said back); the said-back step keeps it safe, but it reads oddly
A yes in words the yes patterns do not know ("That sounds right") drops the moment and the agent reads it; the build may then ask for the moment again
